Record Class Tree<L>

java.lang.Object
java.lang.Record
io.github.ericmedvet.jnb.datastructure.Tree<L>
Type Parameters:
L - the type of labels of nodes
Record Components:
label - the label of the root node of this tree
children - the ordered list of trees being children of the root of this tree
All Implemented Interfaces:
Copyable<Tree<L>>, Sized
public record Tree<L>(L label, List<Tree<L>> children) extends Record implements Sized, Copyable<Tree<L>>
An ordered tree with nodes labeled with non-null labels of type L.

  • Method Details

    • from

      public static <L> Tree<L> from(Function<? super List<Integer>, Optional<? extends L>> lineageMapper)
      Builds a tree from a function that maps lineages to labels. For building the new tree, this method invokes the function lineageMapper repeatedly starting from the root (i.e., with lineage []). For every higher branch, it invokes the lineageMapper starting from the index 0 and stops, for that level, when the mapper returns an empty optional. The method invokes the function in a depth first way.
      Type Parameters:
      L - the type of labels of nodes
      Parameters:
      lineageMapper - a function that takes a lineage (see descendant(List)) and returns the label that is to be used in the new tree at that lineage
      Returns:
      the built tree
      Throws:
      IllegalArgumentException - if the lineageMapper gives an empty Optional for the empty lineage [], which should instead give the label of the root

      public Tree<L> descendant(int... lineage)
      Returns the tree being located at the given lineage coordinate. Internally, it calls descendant(List).
      Parameters:
      lineage - the sequence of zero-based indexes to look at in this tree
      Returns:
      the tree at the given lineage, if any
      Throws:
      IndexOutOfBoundsException - if there is no child at one of the indexes of the provided lineage

    • descendant

      public Tree<L> descendant(List<Integer> lineage)
      Returns the tree being located at the given lineage coordinate. A lineage coordinate, simply lineage, is a sequence of zero-based indexes identifying the child to choose starting from the root of this tree. The empty lineage [] refers to this tree. The [0] lineage represents the first child of this tree. The [1,0] lineage represents the first child of the second child of this tree.
      Parameters:
      lineage - the sequence of zero-based indexes to look at in this tree
      Returns:
      the tree at the given lineage, if any
      Throws:
      IndexOutOfBoundsException - if there is no child at one of the indexes of the provided lineage

    • lineages

      public SequencedSet<List<Integer>> lineages()
      Returns all the lineages (see descendant(List)) of this tree, in a depth first predictable order. A copy of this tree can be rebuilt from the returned lineages through the from(Function) method, namely with from(l -> Optional.of(descendant(l).label())).
      Returns:
      all the lineages of this tree

    • toString

      public String toString()
      Returns a string representation of this tree. It is built recursively by concatenating this tree label followed by, if this is not a leaf node, "("<L>, the list of children string representations separated by ";"<L>, and ")"<L>.
      Specified by:
      toString in class Record
      Returns:
      a string representation of this tree
